source_text: πνεύματος ἁγίου γεγεννῆσθαι. ἐπειδή, ὡς εἴρηται, καὶ τὴν ἀρχὴν συμπαρῆν τὸ προαιώνιον καὶ προκόσμιον πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ ποιητῇ τῆς ἡμετέρας φύσεως, οὐχ ὡς χρῄζοντι βοηθείας, ἀλλὰ σὺν ταυτότητι καὶ ἰσότητι θεότητος καὶ θελήσεως, καὶ οἷον μὴ ἀποτετμημένον τοῦ φωτὸς τὸ φῶς. ἢ σύσθητι οὖν, Μακεδόνιε, τοῖς ἁγίοις, κτίσμα τὸ θεῖον πνεῦμα μὴ ὀνομάζουσιν, ἀλλ' ἐκπεπορεῦσθαι ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ κατὰ φύσιν· ἤ, ὡς ἔθος σοι φάσκειν, ὅτι θεοῦ μὲν ἥττων τῇ φύσει, ἀγγέλων δὲ κρείττων ἐστίν, μέσην τινὰ φύσιν καὶ τάξιν εἰληχός, ἀπόδειξον κεχρησμῳδηκότας· τὰ γὰρ ἐκείνων δικαίως προτετίμηται παρὰ τῷ θεῷ τῶν σῶν καὶ τῶν Ἀρείου· καὶ οὐχ ὡς δίδωσιν ὁ τῆς τέχνης καὶ τῆς σοφιστείας νόμος, ἐξόν σοι θαρρήσαντι ἀφεῖναι κατὰ τοῦ θείου πνεύματος ἰδίους λόγους· οὗ τὴν θείαν φύσιν οὐδ' ἂν εἰ τοὺς τῆς διανοίας ὀφθαλμοὺς τοσούτους καὶ τοιούτους εἶχες, ὅσους καὶ οἵους ἔδωκεν ἡ γραφὴ τοῖς χερουβίμ, ἠδυνήθης ἂν κἂν ποσῶς γοῦν θεωρῆσαι. τίς γὰρ ἐπιδράττεται τῆς ἀφανοῦς καὶ ἀχωρήτου θεότητος; ἢ καταγνοὺς τῆς σεαυτοῦ ἀσεβείας εἴκων ἡμῖν τῶν πρωτείων ἀφίστασο. 7.4ν ὅτι ἁγιάζει καὶ δικαιοῖ 7.4 ἀλλ' ἐπανίωμεν πάλιν ἐπὶ τὴν ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὑπόθεσιν, ὅτι ἁγιάζει καὶ δικαιοῖ καθὰ προείπομεν. 7.5ν ὅτι σωτηρίαν χορηγεῖ ὅτι σωτηρίαν καὶ τοῖς ἀποσφαλεῖσιν χορηγεῖ· ὃ μόνης ἐστὶν τῆς παγκρατορικῆς οὐσίας. ἄνευ γὰρ θεοῦ πρᾶξαί τι κτιστόν, ἀμήχανον. «οὐδ' ὅσον ἀμπετάσαι βλεφαρῶν περιφαέα κύκλα.» ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ ἀπόστολος Φιλιππησίοις τοιάδε· «οἶδα γάρ, ὅτι τοῦτό μοι ἀποβήσεται εἰς σωτηρίαν, διὰ τῆς ὑμῶν δεήσεως καὶ ἐπιχορηγίας τοῦ πνεύματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.» καθὰ ὕμνηται περὶ μὲν τοῦ πατρὸς ἐν Ὠσηέ· «πλὴν ἐμοῦ οὐ γνώσῃ· καὶ σώζων οὐκ ἔστιν πάρεξ ἐμοῦ·» περὶ δὲ τοῦ υἱοῦ ἐν ταῖς πράξεσιν· «καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἄλλῳ οὐδενὶ ἡ σωτηρία. οὐδὲ γὰρ ἄλλο ὄνομά ἐστιν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸ δεδομένον ἐν ἀνθρώποις, ἐν ᾧ δεῖ σωθῆναι.» 7.6ν ὅτι θανάτου ἐλευθεροῖ καὶ ἁμαρτίας συγχωρεῖ ὅτι θανάτου ἐλευθεροῖ καὶ ἁμαρτίας συγχωρεῖ, ἅτε δὴ ἐκ τῆς πατρικῆς ῥίζης οὐσίας καρπὸν φέρον τὸ ἀθάνατον καὶ ἵλεω. κτίσματι δὲ οὐ δυνατὸν ἢ ἀναμάρτητον εἶναι ἢ ἓν τούτων οἴκοθεν ποιῆσαι. οὐδὲ γὰρ οὐδὲν τῶν πνευμάτων, ὡς προεδείχθη, ἀναμάρτητον· οὐδὲ τάχα, καθ' ὑπερβολὴν λόγου, ἡ μὴ οὖσα λογική. καὶ γὰρ ὁ οὐρανὸς αὐτὸς καὶ ὁ ἥλιος πρὸς τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ καθαρότητα οὐκ ἄμεμπτοι. εἰ γὰρ καὶ φαίνονται ἀπόστολοί ποτε τοιοῦτόν τι πράξαντες, οὐκ ἰδίᾳ δυνάμει περιεγένοντο, ἀλλὰ τῇ τοῦ εἰπόντος· «ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ὀνόματι μείζονα τούτων ποιήσετε·» καὶ τῇ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ πατρὸς τοῦ λαλήσαντος ἐν αὐτοῖς, καθὰ Ῥωμαίους Παῦλος διδάσκει· «ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν με ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου.» καὶ ὁ δεσπότης δὲ παρ' Ἰωάννῃ, ἀποδιδοὺς ἡμῖν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, ὁ ἀπολέσαντες ἦμεν διὰ τῆς ἀρχαίας παρακοῆς, ἐνεφύσησεν εἰς τὰ πρόσωπα τῶν μαθητῶν καὶ εἶπεν· «λάβετε πνεῦμα ἅγιον. ἄν τινων ἀφῆτε τὰς ἁμαρτίας, ἀφίενται· ἄν τινων κρατῆτε, κεκράτηνται.» ἐνταῦθα τοσοῦτον τοῦ ἀειμνήστου πνεύματος τὸ αὐτεξούσιον, ὅτι αὐτό τε δι' ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτίας συγχωρεῖ, καὶ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι καὶ τῇ δυνάμει αὐτοῦ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ πάντες οἱ πιστεύοντες αὐτῷ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν παρέχουσιν. ὅτι δὲ θεοῦ μόνου τὸ ἱλάσκεσθαι ἁμαρτάνουσιν, ἔνδοξοι θεοῦ ῥήσεις σημαίνουσιν· «ἐγώ», γάρ φησιν, «εἰμὶ ὁ ἐξαλείφων τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου», καί· «ἐὰν ὦσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ὑμῶν ὡς φοινικοῦν, ὡς χίονα λευκανῶ· ἐὰν δὲ ὦσιν ὡς κόκκινον, ὡσεὶ ἔριον λευκανῶ.» καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ δὲ ὡς παῖς θεοῦ τῷ παραλύτῳ ἔφη· «τέκνον, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι», καί· «ἴδε ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ αἴρων τὰς 73 ἁμαρτίας τοῦ κόσμου.» 7.7ν ὅτι συνεργεῖ τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ· καὶ ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ πνεύματος σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἐποίησεν καὶ δαιμόνια ἐξέβαλεν διὰ τὸ
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: ... but we rather confirm this by saying that from] the Holy Spirit he was born. Since, as has been said, also at the beginning the Spirit of God, before the ages and before the world, was present together with the maker of our nature, not as to one needing help, but with sameness and equality of Godhead and of will, and like light not cut off from light. Either, then, agree, Macedonian, with the saints, who do not name the divine Spirit a creature, but [say] that it has proceeded from God, as his Spirit by nature; or, as is your custom to assert, that it is lesser than God in nature but greater than angels, having obtained by lot some middle nature and rank, show [them] having declared [this] by oracle; for their [words] have justly been honoured before God above yours and those of Arius; and [it is] not, as the law of the art and of sophistry grants, permitted to you, having grown bold, to let loose your own words against the divine Spirit; whose divine nature, not even if you had the eyes of the mind as many and such as Scripture gave to the cherubim, would you have been able to contemplate even in some small degree. For who lays hold of the invisible and uncontainable Godhead? Or, having condemned your own impiety, yielding to us, stand away from the first prizes. 7.4ν [Chapter title:] That it sanctifies and justifies. 7.4 But let us go back again to the subject from the beginning, that it sanctifies and justifies, as we said before. 7.5ν [Chapter title:] That it supplies salvation. That it supplies salvation also to those who have slipped away; which belongs to the almighty essence alone. For without God it is impossible for a created [thing] to do anything, 'not even so much as to spread open the shining circles of the eyelids.' For the apostle used to say to the Philippians such things: 'For I know that this will turn out for me for salvation through your entreaty and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.' Just as it is hymned about the Father in Hosea: 'Besides me you will not know [another]; and there is none saving except me'; and about the Son in the Acts: 'And salvation is in no other one. For neither is there another name under heaven that is given among men, in which it is necessary to be saved.' 7.6ν [Chapter title:] That it frees from death and forgives sins. That it frees from death and forgives sins, inasmuch as from the paternal root of essence it bears as fruit the immortal and the merciful. But for a creature it is not possible either to be sinless or to do one of these things from its own house. For not any one of the spirits, as was shown before, is sinless; nor perhaps, by excess of speech, the [creation] that is not rational. For indeed heaven itself and the sun, toward the purity of God, are not blameless. For even if apostles appear at some time to have done some such thing, they did not prevail by their own power, but by that of the one who said: 'in my name you will do greater things than these'; and by that of the Spirit of the Father who spoke in them, as Paul teaches the Romans: 'For the law of the Spirit in Christ Jesus freed me from the law of sin and of death.' And the Master also, in John, giving back to us the Holy Spirit, which we had lost through the ancient disobedience, breathed into the faces of the disciples and said: 'Receive Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven; if you retain those of any, they are retained.' Here so great is the self-determining authority of the ever-remembered Spirit, that it both through itself forgives sins, and in its name and power the apostles and all who believe in it provide forgiveness of sins. And that to be propitious to those who sin belongs to God alone, glorious sayings of God signify: 'I,' for he says, 'am the one blotting out your sins'; and: 'if your sins are as crimson, I will whiten [them] as snow; and if they are as scarlet, I will whiten [them] as wool.' And the Saviour also, as Child of God, said to the paralytic: 'child, your sins are forgiven you'; and: 'behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the [page number 73, debris] sins of the world.' 7.7ν [Chapter title:] That it works together with the Father and the Son; and that Christ in the power of the Spirit made signs and wonders and cast out demons because of the [continues in the next section] ...
pass_b_english: …of the Holy Spirit he was born. For, as has been said, at the beginning too the Spirit of God, who is before the ages and before the world, was present with the maker of our nature, not as with one who needed help, but in sameness and equality of Godhead and of will, like light not cut off from light.

So, Macedonian, either agree with the saints, who do not call the divine Spirit a creature but say that he has proceeded from God, as his Spirit by nature; or else, since it is your habit to claim that he is lesser than God by nature but greater than the angels, having been allotted some middle nature and rank, show us that the saints have declared this as an oracle. For their words are rightly honoured by God above yours and above those of Arius. You are not free, as the law of rhetorical art and of sophistry allows, to grow bold and let fly arguments of your own against the divine Spirit. You could not have caught sight of his divine nature in even the smallest measure, not even if you had eyes of the mind as many and of such a kind as Scripture gave to the cherubim. For who can lay hold of the invisible Godhead that nothing can contain? Or else condemn your own impiety, give way to us, and withdraw from the contest for first place.
But let us come back again to the subject we began with: that he sanctifies and justifies, as we said before.

He supplies salvation even to those who have gone astray, and this belongs to the almighty essence alone. For without God it is impossible for a created thing to do anything, “not even so much as to open the bright circles of the eyelids.” For the Apostle spoke to the Philippians in these words: “For I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your prayer and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:19). So it is sung of the Father in Hosea: “Besides me you shall know no other, and there is none who saves except me” (Hosea 13:4); and of the Son in the Acts: “And there is salvation in no one else. For there is no other name under heaven given among men by which one must be saved” (Acts 4:12).
That he frees from death and forgives sins.

He frees from death and forgives sins, since from the root of the Father’s essence he bears immortality and mercy as his fruit. But a creature cannot either be sinless or do one of these things by its own power. For none of the spirits, as was shown earlier, is sinless; nor perhaps, to put it in the strongest terms, is the creation that is not rational. For even heaven itself and the sun are not blameless beside the purity of God.

For even if apostles at times appear to have done some such thing, they did not prevail by their own power, but by the power of him who said, “In my name you will do greater things than these” (John 14:12), and by the power of the Spirit of the Father who spoke in them (Matthew 10:20), as Paul teaches the Romans: “For the law of the Spirit in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and of death” (Romans 8:2). And in John the Master, giving back to us the Holy Spirit whom we had lost through the ancient disobedience, breathed into the faces of the disciples and said: “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven; if you retain the sins of any, they are retained” (John 20:22–23). Here the sovereign freedom of the ever-remembered Spirit is so great that he both forgives sins by himself, and in his name and by his power the apostles and all who believe in him grant forgiveness of sins.

That it belongs to God alone to show mercy to sinners, glorious sayings of God make plain. “I,” he says, “am he who blots out your sins” (Isaiah 43:25); and, “If your sins are like crimson, I will make them white as snow; and if they are like scarlet, I will make them white as wool” (Isaiah 1:18). And the Saviour too, as the Son of God, said to the paralytic, “Child, your sins are forgiven you” (Mark 2:5); and, “Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world” (John 1:29).

choices.issue: Garbled machine draft, misplaced Hosea, chapter titles run into the text
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u18): retranslated. The old English began 'To have been begotten of the Holy Spirit' as a sentence, wrote 'establish this with the holy ones', 'honored by the God of yours and of Arius', 'you would have been able to behold it, how much more so' (the Greek says he could not), 'you stand apart from the first ones', 'Nor even as to grape-harvesting with eyes circling', 'concerning the Father in the Psalms' for Hosea 13:4, 'exceeding the word, is the non-existent rational [being]', 'who had lost us', 'unremembered Spirit' and 'as a child of God'; it merged the chapter titles 7.4, 7.5, 7.6 and 7.7 into the body. References: (Rom 8:2), (Isa 43:25), (Isa 1:18) written in full; Hosea 13:4 now attributed to Hosea as the Greek says; Matthew 10:20 added. Brackets [must be saved], [Spirit], [being] removed.

choices.english: …of the Holy Spirit he was born.
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence (the previous section ends 'by saying that from'); only the words this section holds are translated, opened with '…'.
The form is odd (perhaps for συντέθητι or σύνθου, 'agree'); the either/or that follows needs 'agree with the saints'. Flagged in problems.

choices.english: show us that the saints have declared this as an oracle
choices.why: The accusative participle refers back to the saints: Macedonius must prove that inspired Scripture says the Spirit has a middle rank.

choices.english: withdraw from the contest for first place
choices.why: τὰ πρωτεῖα are the first prizes of a contest; Didymus tells his opponent to concede the match.

choices.term: ὅτι σωτηρίαν καὶ τοῖς ἀποσφαλεῖσιν χορηγεῖ
choices.english: He supplies salvation even to those who have gone astray
choices.why: The body repeats the chapter title in outline form with ὅτι; English states it as a sentence so the title is not printed twice word for word.

choices.term: οὐδ' ὅσον ἀμπετάσαι βλεφαρῶν περιφαέα κύκλα
choices.english: not even so much as to open the bright circles of the eyelids
choices.why: A hexameter line quoted as proverbial verse, not Scripture; kept in quotation marks without a reference. Source not identified; flagged in problems.

choices.english: Besides me you shall know no other
choices.why: The LXX of Hosea 13:4 implies 'god'; 'no other' supplies the object English needs without adding a claim. The Greek says 'in Hosea', so the old 'in the Psalms' was wrong.

choices.term: καρπὸν φέρον τὸ ἀθάνατον καὶ ἵλεω
choices.english: he bears immortality and mercy as his fruit
choices.why: The neuter adjectives are the fruit the Spirit bears from the Father's essence; they ground the two titles, freeing from death and forgiving.
Literally 'from its own house', of itself; matches 'not by their own power' in the next paragraph.

choices.english: to put it in the strongest terms
choices.why: Didymus marks the claim that irrational creation is not sinless as a hyperbole.

choices.english: the creation that is not rational
choices.why: The feminine implies κτίσις; contrasted with the rational spirits just named.

choices.term: τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ πατρὸς τοῦ λαλήσαντος ἐν αὐτοῖς
choices.english: the Spirit of the Father who spoke in them (Matthew 10:20)
choices.why: Clear allusion to Matthew 10:20, 'the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you'; cited inline.
The Spirit's own authority to forgive, not a creature's free choice.
Didymus' honorific for the Spirit; the old 'unremembered' reversed it.
παῖς can mean child or servant; the argument is that the Saviour forgives as God does, so 'Son' fits Didymus' point.
Didymus adds the Baptist's words about the Saviour with a bare 'and'; English keeps the bare 'and' rather than putting them in the Saviour's mouth.
73 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped.
The chapter title 7.7 runs into the next section (ἀχώριστον τῆς θεότητος, 'inseparability of the Godhead'); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
